title: AI Capability Manifest
description: Metadata contract describing one independently adoptable AI capability (Mission 4, Manifest v0.1 draft, revised in place on 2026-10-23 from the Spikes 1-3 research). It describes a capability; it is not a runtime execution protocol, and it references native contracts (MCP, A2A, OpenAPI, SKILL.md) instead of restating them. Mission 4 owns this structure and its rules; the content of each manifest belongs to the capability's owners and the inventory owners. Only facts that every sampled source supplies are mandatory; the validator reports the completeness level a manifest reaches (x-completenessLevels) instead of requiring more. Omitted optional fields mean 'not provided' and null is never allowed; an explicit empty list means 'declared none'. Top-level fields prefixed with 'x-' are extension fields that core consumers ignore.

schemaVersion.description: Version (MAJOR.MINOR) of the manifest schema this document conforms to. Selects the validation contract; it is not the version of the capability.
schemaVersion.x-hint: Use schemaVersion: "0.1" (quoted MAJOR.MINOR). Unquoted 0.1 is read by YAML as a number, and patch versions such as "0.1.0" are not used.

id.description: Stable, unique capability identifier '<namespace>/<name>'. Assigned once by the catalog or the contribution workflow and never changed or reused, even if the repository, owner, or name changes. Never derived from a native name or a URL: those are recorded in source and publications.

name.description: Human-readable display name. Not an identifier and not required to be unique.
name.x-hint: Use a short display name of 3-80 characters without leading or trailing spaces, e.g. 'SQL Review'.

description.description: What the capability does and the problem it solves. Required for the 'discoverable' completeness level; when the native metadata has none (some catalog entries do not), a curator writes it.
examples: Reviews SQL changes in pull requests for performance anti-patterns and data-access policy violations.
description.x-hint: Describe the capability's purpose and functionality in 20-1024 characters.

capabilityType.description: Capability classification. 'framework' and 'platform' cover the frameworks and platforms that the capability landscape catalogues. Prompts, commands, hooks, and resources are modelled as embeddedComponents of a parent capability, not as capability types.
capabilityType.x-hint: Use one of the capability types defined by the schema (lowercase snake_case).

capabilityVersion.description: Version of the capability itself, when its owner versions it with Semantic Versioning 2.0.0; the compatibility check uses it. Independent of schemaVersion. Native versions in other schemes (PEP 440, commit pins, tags), and the versions of individual publications, go in publications[].nativeVersion.
capabilityVersion.x-hint: Use a quoted Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 version such as "1.3.0" (no 'v' prefix), or omit it and record the native version per publication.

source.description: Primary reference to where the capability is maintained or obtained: repository, registry entry, provider, or other reference. A source is a location, not an identity. Other channels that distribute the same capability go in publications.

publications.description: Channels that distribute this same capability, each with its native name, version, and status: registry entries, packages, container images, marketplace entries, hosted endpoints. One capability is often published several times with different names and versions; listing them is what lets consumers recognise it across sources.
publications.x-hint: Provide a list of publications, each with 'kind' and 'locator', e.g. '- { kind: package, locator: "pkg:npm/%40example-org/runbook-search" }'.

owner.description: Responsible owner, maintaining entity, or verified publisher. Required for the 'assessable' completeness level; its contact is required for 'adoptable'.

license.description: License or terms of use, as an SPDX expression where one is stated, with the scope it was stated for. Required for the 'assessable' completeness level.

documentation.description: Link to the capability's documentation or home page.

keywords.description: Search terms, tags, or categories, as native formats state them. They help discovery but are not a controlled vocabulary.
keywords.x-hint: Provide a list of short search terms, e.g. '- sql'.

lifecycleStatus.description: Lifecycle state declared by the capability's owner, which also expresses its availability. Independent of maturity, risk classification, and approval status. Statuses observed in channels (a registry status, a deprecation message, an archived repository) are recorded per publication in publications[].status. Expectations for approval, monitoring, reassessment, and retirement are defined by the governance framework (Mission 3), not by this field.
lifecycleStatus.x-hint: Use one of the lifecycle states defined by the schema, or omit the field if the owner has not declared one.

maturity.description: Evidence of real-world use, independent of lifecycleStatus (availability). prototype: demonstrated, not yet used for real work; pilot: used for real work by a limited group under evaluation; production: used in production and supported for broader adoption. Values are assigned by the inventory owners (Mission 2); the level definitions are proposals to agree with them.
maturity.x-hint: Use one of the maturity levels defined by the schema, or omit the field if maturity is not known.

riskTier.description: Risk classification or assessment state. 'unassessed' means no risk assessment is recorded and must never be interpreted as low risk or approval. A risk tier is not an approval. The classification vocabulary is owned by the governance framework (Mission 3); the tier names here are placeholders until it is agreed.
riskTier.x-hint: Use 'unassessed' when no risk assessment has been completed; an assessed tier (low, medium, high) also requires assessmentReference.

assessmentReference.description: Reference to the risk assessment record that produced riskTier.

lastUpdated.description: Date the manifest metadata was last updated (ISO 8601 calendar date). It is the date of this record, not the date the capability changed: that date is recorded per publication in publications[].updatedAt.

deprecation.description: Deprecation details: reason, optional replacement, and optional sunset date.

supportedUseCases.description: Use cases the capability is intended to support.
supportedUseCases.x-hint: Provide a list of use cases, each with a 'title', e.g. '- title: Review SQL in pull requests'.

intendedAudience.description: Roles or groups the capability is intended for, for example 'backend engineers' or 'data analysts'.
intendedAudience.x-hint: Provide a list of audiences, e.g. '- backend engineers'.

interfaces.description: How consumers interact with the capability. Protocol-native contracts (MCP, A2A Agent Card, OpenAPI) are referenced, not duplicated. Required for the 'discoverable' completeness level.
interfaces.x-hint: Provide a list of interfaces, each with a 'type' (for example mcp, a2a, openapi, agent_skill, cli).

runtime.description: Where and on what the capability runs: a local process, a container, a hosted service, an agent host, or a CI runner. Required for the 'assessable' completeness level.
runtime.x-hint: Provide a list of runtime environments, each with a 'kind', e.g. '- { kind: local_process, detail: Node.js >=18 }'.

setup.description: What an adopter must provide before the capability works: credentials, environment variables, accounts, or configuration. An empty list declares that nothing is needed; omit the field when this is not known. Required for the 'adoptable' completeness level.
setup.x-hint: Provide a list of setup items, each with a 'name', e.g. '- { name: GITHUB_TOKEN, secret: true, required: true }', or [] to declare that nothing is needed.

platformCompatibility.description: Platforms, hosts, or clients the capability is known to work with, as lowercase kebab-case tokens (for example 'vs-code', 'github-actions', 'linux'). The token vocabulary is not yet controlled.
platformCompatibility.x-hint: Use lowercase kebab-case platform tokens, e.g. 'github-actions'.

dependencies.description: Other capabilities this capability requires, referenced by id. An empty list declares that there are none.
dependencies.x-hint: Provide a list of capability references, e.g. '- id: sre/runbook-search', or [] to declare none.

limitations.description: Known limitations and constraints relevant to adopters. An empty list declares that none are known. Required for the 'adoptable' completeness level.
limitations.x-hint: Provide a list of short statements, or [] to declare none.

costInformation.description: How use of the capability is paid for, where known. Consumers that weigh cost read it; omit it when the cost model is unknown.

components.description: Independently adoptable child capabilities, each with its own manifest, referenced by id.
components.x-hint: Provide a list of child capability references, e.g. '- id: sre/runbook-search'.

embeddedComponents.description: Parts of this capability that are not independently adoptable (prompts, commands, hooks, resources) and therefore have no manifest of their own.
embeddedComponents.x-hint: Provide a list of components, each with 'name' and 'type'.

parent.description: Parent capability (bundle) this independently adoptable component belongs to.

relations.description: How this capability relates to other capabilities that are not its dependencies, components, or replacement: forks, wrappers, derivatives, other catalog entries for the same capability, and look-alikes that are different capabilities.
relations.x-hint: Provide a list of relations, each with a 'type' and an 'id' or 'locator', e.g. '- { type: fork_of, id: microsoft/playwright-mcp }'.

provenance.description: Where values in this manifest come from, per field: stated by the capability's native metadata, read from a source it declares, derived by a rule, declared by the owner, or curated. A value without an entry is unattributed. A value derived by a heuristic should be confirmed before it is relied on.
provenance.x-hint: Provide a list of entries, each with 'field' (a JSON Pointer), 'method', and 'source', e.g. '- { field: /license, method: native, source: npm package.json license }'.

^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$.description: Extension field. Accepted without validation and ignored by core consumers.

allOf.description: An assessed riskTier must cite the assessment that produced it, so that a tier cannot be self-asserted.
allOf.x-hint: Add assessmentReference with the assessment record id (for example 'id: RA-2026-0142'), or set riskTier to 'unassessed' if no assessment has been completed.

allOf.description: A deprecated or retired capability must record why, so that adopters can plan a migration.
allOf.x-hint: Add a deprecation block with a 'reason' (and 'replacedBy' if a replacement exists), or correct lifecycleStatus.

allOf.description: An mcp_server must declare at least one interface whose type is 'mcp'.
allOf.x-hint: Add an interface entry with 'type: mcp' to interfaces.

x-completenessLevels.description: It can be found and recognised: the mandatory fields, plus what it does and how it is used.
A reuse assessment can start: where it runs, its terms, its version, a lifecycle signal, and who owns or publishes it. Usually reachable from native metadata alone.
A team can adopt it without asking: the setup it needs, how to reach its owner, and its limitations (an empty list declares none). Needs owner input.
A risk assessment is recorded: an assessed riskTier, which must cite its assessmentReference. Set by the governance owners (Mission 3), never inferred.

capabilityId.description: Capability identifier '<namespace>/<name>': lowercase kebab-case segments that may start with a digit (registry-verified namespaces such as io.github.0xmortuex do); the namespace may contain dot-separated segments.
capabilityId.x-hint: Use a lowercase, namespaced id '<namespace>/<name>' in kebab-case, e.g. 'ai-platform/sql-review'.

date.x-hint: Use a quoted ISO 8601 calendar date YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-10-19".

observedStatus.x-hint: Use one of the observed statuses defined by the schema, or omit the field if the source reports none.

capabilityRef.x-hint: Reference a capability by id, e.g. 'id: sre/runbook-search'.

type.x-hint: Use one of the source types defined by the schema.

path.description: Location of the capability inside the repository (monorepos), relative to the repository root.
path.x-hint: Use a relative path without a leading slash, e.g. 'skills/sql-review'.

repositoryId.description: The forge's stable id for the repository at url (for example GitHub's numeric repository id). It stays the same when the repository is renamed or moved and changes when a repository is deleted and recreated under the same name, so it links records that cite an old URL.
repositoryId.x-hint: Use the forge's repository id as a quoted string, e.g. "952688112".

status.description: Lifecycle status that the source reports (an observed signal, for example a repository the forge reports as archived). Independent of lifecycleStatus, which the owner declares.

updatedAt.description: Date of the latest change at the source: the last commit to the capability's path, or the last push to its repository when the capability is the whole repository. It is the date the capability changed there, not the date the manifest changed.

registry.description: Registry that distributes the capability (for example npm, pypi, mcp-registry).
registry.x-hint: Use a lowercase registry name such as 'npm' or 'pypi'.

identifier.description: Package or entry identifier within the registry.

description.description: How to obtain the capability when no other source type applies.

allOf.description: A repository source must provide the repository URL.
allOf.x-hint: Add 'url' with the repository's https:// URL.

allOf.description: A registry source must name the registry and the package identifier.
allOf.x-hint: Add 'registry' (for example npm) and 'identifier' (the package name).

allOf.description: A provider source must provide the provider's URL.
allOf.x-hint: Add 'url' with the provider's https:// URL, for example its product documentation.

allOf.description: An 'other' source must describe how the capability is obtained.
allOf.x-hint: Add 'description' explaining how to obtain the capability.

source.x-hint: Provide a source block with a 'type' (repository, registry, provider, or other) and its location.

kind.description: Kind of channel: an entry in a registry or catalog (the MCP Registry, the Docker MCP catalog); a package (npm, PyPI); a container image; an entry in a plugin marketplace; a hosted endpoint; a repository from which the capability is used directly (Agent Skills, GitHub Actions); or other.
kind.x-hint: Use one of the publication kinds defined by the schema.

locator.description: Where to find the publication, in the form its channel uses: a Package URL for packages (pkg:npm/%40playwright/mcp), an image reference without a tag (docker.io/mcp/playwright), a registry name (io.github.microsoft/playwright-mcp), a marketplace coordinate (playwright@claude-plugins-official), or an https URL. Consumers compare locators case-insensitively.
locator.x-hint: Use the channel's own coordinates without spaces, e.g. a Package URL such as 'pkg:npm/%40example-org/runbook-search'.

nativeName.description: The capability's name in this channel, when it differs from the locator.

nativeVersion.description: Version that this publication states, in its own scheme. Publications of one capability often carry different versions at the same time.

versionScheme.description: Scheme of nativeVersion: Semantic Versioning; PEP 440; a date-based version; a commit pin; a git tag; a floating reference such as 'latest'; 'unversioned' when the channel publishes no version; or other. Versions are compared only when their schemes allow it.
versionScheme.x-hint: Use one of the version schemes defined by the schema.

status.description: Lifecycle status that the channel reports for this publication (an observed signal: the MCP Registry status, npm's deprecation flag, an archived repository, a yanked release). Independent of lifecycleStatus, which the owner declares.

statusMessage.description: Message that accompanies the status, if any (for example npm's deprecation message).

updatedAt.description: Date this publication was last updated in its channel (for example its latest publish date): the date the capability changed there, not the date the manifest changed.

verifiedBy.description: How this publication is known to belong to the capability: a declared back-link (npm mcpName, PyPI mcp-name), the registry's verification of a namespace, a build from the same repository, or a configuration that only runs it. Omit when the link is not verified.

publication.x-hint: Provide each publication with its 'kind' and 'locator', e.g. '- { kind: package, locator: "pkg:npm/%40example-org/runbook-search" }'.

name.description: Owning team, maintaining organization, or verified publisher.
name.x-hint: Name the owning team or maintaining organization.

contact.description: Email address or https URL (for example a support page or an issue tracker) for the owner. Required for the 'adoptable' completeness level.
contact.x-hint: Use an email address (team@example.com) or an https:// URL such as a support page.

affiliation.description: Whether the maintaining entity is internal to the organization or external (vendor, community).

owner.x-hint: Provide an owner block with at least a name, and contact and affiliation (internal or external) where known.

expression.description: SPDX license expression, for example Apache-2.0, MIT OR Apache-2.0, or LicenseRef-<name> for terms that are not on the SPDX License List.
expression.x-hint: Use an SPDX license expression such as 'Apache-2.0' or 'MIT OR Apache-2.0'; put terms that are not an SPDX expression in 'text'.

text.description: The license or terms as stated, when they are not an SPDX expression (for example 'Proprietary', or a pointer to a LICENSE file). Such terms must be read by a person before reuse.

url.description: Link to the full license text or terms.

scope.description: What the license was stated for: 'capability' when it was stated for this capability (for example in its package metadata), 'repository' when it was read from the repository as a whole, which may not cover a capability inside a shared repository.

allOf.description: A license must give an SPDX expression or the terms as text.
allOf.x-hint: Add 'expression' with an SPDX license expression (for example Apache-2.0), or 'text' with the terms as stated.

license.x-hint: Provide license with an SPDX 'expression' (for example 'expression: Apache-2.0'), or 'text' for other terms.

id.description: Identifier of the assessment record in the governance system of record.

assessmentReference.x-hint: Provide assessmentReference with at least the assessment 'id', e.g. 'id: RA-2026-0142'.

reason.description: Why the capability is deprecated or retired.
reason.x-hint: Explain why the capability is deprecated in 10-500 characters.

replacedBy.description: Identifier of the capability that replaces this one, if any.

deprecation.x-hint: Provide a deprecation block with at least a 'reason', and 'replacedBy' if a replacement exists.

model.description: Cost model: free; included in an existing license or contract; subscription; usage-based pricing; internal chargeback; or other.
model.x-hint: Use one of the cost models defined by the schema.

details.description: Free-text cost details, for example the pricing basis or the license that covers use.

url.description: Link to pricing or licensing information.

allOf.description: An 'other' cost model must be explained in details.
allOf.x-hint: Add 'details' describing how use of the capability is paid for.

costInformation.x-hint: Provide costInformation with at least a 'model', for example 'model: subscription'.

title.description: Short statement of the use case.

description.description: Additional detail about the use case.

type.description: Interface or protocol through which the capability is used.
type.x-hint: Use one of the interface types defined by the schema.

specVersion.description: Version of the referenced protocol or specification (for example an MCP revision date).

transport.description: Transport or protocol binding, named as the protocol names it (for example stdio or streamable-http for MCP; JSONRPC, GRPC, or HTTP+JSON for A2A).
transport.x-hint: Use the protocol's own name for the transport, e.g. 'stdio'.

contractRef.description: URL of the protocol-native contract (MCP server metadata, A2A Agent Card, OpenAPI document, SKILL.md).

inputs.description: Summary of accepted inputs, with media types where known; no native format other than A2A states them, so they help discovery most when curated. The authoritative contract is the one referenced by contractRef.

outputs.description: Summary of produced outputs, with media types where known. The authoritative contract is the one referenced by contractRef.

allOf.description: A2A and OpenAPI interfaces must reference their native contract (Agent Card or OpenAPI document) instead of re-describing it.
allOf.x-hint: Add 'contractRef' with the https:// URL of the Agent Card or OpenAPI document.

name.description: Name of the input or output.

mediaType.description: IANA media type, for example application/json.
mediaType.x-hint: Use a media type such as 'application/json' or 'text/markdown'.

description.description: What the input or output contains.

kind.description: local_process: runs on the adopter's machine (for example through npx or uvx); container: runs from a container image; hosted_service: runs as a service that someone hosts; agent_host: runs inside an agent host that loads it (an Agent Skill, a plugin); ci_runner: runs in a CI system (a GitHub Action); other.
kind.x-hint: Use one of the runtime kinds defined by the schema.

runtimeEnvironment.x-hint: Provide each runtime environment with a 'kind', e.g. 'kind: local_process'.

name.description: What must be provided: an environment variable (for example GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN), a header, an account, or a setting.

description.description: What it is for and where to get it.

secret.description: true when the value is a credential that must be kept secret.

required.description: true when the capability does not work without it.

setupItem.x-hint: Provide each setup item with a 'name', e.g. 'name: GITHUB_TOKEN'.

type.description: same_as: another catalog entry describes this same capability; fork_of: this capability is a fork of the target; wraps: this capability only configures or packages the target; derived_from: this capability copies or rewrites the target with changes; distinct_from: the target looks the same (same name or description) but is a different capability.
type.x-hint: Use one of the relation types defined by the schema.

id.description: Identifier of the related capability, when it has a manifest.

locator.description: Where the related capability is published, when it has no manifest: a registry name, a Package URL, or an https URL.

evidence.description: What the relation is based on, for example "npm description: 'Fork of official Playwright MCP'".

verified.description: true when the relation was confirmed (for example by the forge's fork record or by the related capability's owner); omitted or false when it is only claimed or inferred.

allOf.description: A relation must identify its target by id or by locator.
allOf.x-hint: Add 'id' with the related capability's id, or 'locator' with where it is published.

relation.x-hint: Provide each relation with a 'type' and an 'id' or 'locator'.

field.description: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) to the value this entry describes, for example /license or /publications/1/nativeVersion.
field.x-hint: Use a JSON Pointer such as '/license' or '/owner/name'.

method.description: native: stated by the capability's own metadata document; linked: read from a source that document declares (for example its repository on the forge); derived: inferred by a rule; owner: declared by the capability owner; curated: entered by a curator.
method.x-hint: Use one of the provenance methods defined by the schema.

basis.description: For derived values: 'convention' when a rule that the source documents and enforces yields the value (a SKILL.md is a skill; the MCP Registry verifies namespaces), 'heuristic' when the value is inferred from wording or context and must be confirmed.

source.description: The field, document, rule, or person the value comes from, for example 'npm package.json license'.

observedAt.description: Date the value was read or declared.

confirmedBy.description: Who confirmed a derived value, if anyone.

allOf.description: A derived value must state its basis, so that heuristic values can be told apart from values that follow from a documented convention.

provenanceEntry.x-hint: Provide each provenance entry with 'field', 'method', and 'source'.

name.description: Component name, unique within the parent capability.

type.x-hint: Use one of the embedded component types defined by the schema.
